subject: Finova POC: First-week hands-on lab & load run scheduling
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@finova.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Finova POC: First-week hands-on lab & load run scheduling

Hi Anna —

Following our intake call, I’d like to lock in the week-one hands-on sessions so we can progress to the load validation. Proposed plan below — let me know if this aligns with Finova’s stakeholders and availability: 

1) Kickoff + introductions (30m) — review goals & success criteria, confirm roles (PO, Eng lead, Security)
2) Prompt review & routing walkthrough (60m) — share prompt set, expected routing/policy behaviors, test cases
3) Parallel: live lab (workbench access) + load window (2 hours) — run 1k RPS synthetic traffic with prefixes/cache warmup
4) Post-run debrief (30m) — basic perf/quality observations, next steps for tuning/quantization

Success criteria we typically validate in-week 1:
- Functional routing for at least the 3 main prompt flows
- Endpoint p95 latency under 200ms for non-batched short completions (target)
- Load run with <1% error rate at the agreed RPS
- Prompt fidelity: sample pass-rate >=95% on the initial eval set

Suggested windows (PDT):
- Kickoff + intros: Mon 2026-05-25 10:00–10:30
- Prompt review: Mon 2026-05-25 10:45–11:45
- Load window: Tue 2026-05-26 14:00–16:00 (2-hr slot)
- Debrief: Tue 2026-05-26 16:15–16:45

Can you confirm stakeholder names/roles and whether the proposed slots work? Also, could Finova share the initial prompt bank (redacted if needed) and an IP allowlist for our test endpoints before the run?

Attachments: poc-week1-agenda.xlsx (outline + checklist)

Thanks!

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

Thanks — that plan looks good. Quick confirmations from our side:

- The times you suggested are fine; prefer Mon kickoff at 10:00 PT.
- We will share a redacted prompt set by Monday morning and an IP allowlist for test endpoints.

One ask: Priya requested a short pre-read on data handling and where logs/audit trails will be available during the run (SOC2 scope). Can you include the checklist or a pointer?

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Finova POC: First-week hands-on lab & load run scheduling

Camila / Marissa —

Thanks Anna for the quick turnaround. A couple of internal notes so we’re ready:
- Pre-run checklist: ensure Finova prompt set mapped to our routing tags; we’ll stage a routing policy that mirrors expected production traffic (priority tags: billing, account_lookup, narrative).
- Load harness: we’ll run two warm-up phases (prefix load + KV warm cache) ~20 minutes total before the 2-hour run, then three ramp steps to 1k RPS.
- Monitoring: Marissa — please prepare the console dashboards (token breakdown, p95, error rates) and set an alert for error rate >0.5% during the run.
- Security: provide the short SOC2 pre-read link and any IP ranges. Anna, if Priya wants a short runbook for audit logs export, we can include that in the drive link.

I’ll block a candidate calendar and coordinate with infra to reserve the nodes for Tue 14:00–16:30 PT (padding).

—Diego
